ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, $\triangle ABC$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$, $CD$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, $\angle BCD=56^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect $BD$, \\
since $CD$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, \\
thus $\angle DBC=90^\circ$, \\
since $\angle BCD=56^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle BDC=90^\circ-56^\circ=34^\circ$, \\
since $\overset{\frown}{BC}=\overset{\frown}{BC}$, \\
thus $\angle A=\boxed{34^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing O at the center on diameter CD, with B and C on the circle and A also on the circle. From the text, use ∠BCD = 56° and CD as a diameter, so ray CO is the same line as ray CD; hence ∠BCO = 56°. Since OB and OC are radii, triangle BOC is isosceles, so ∠OBC = 56°. Therefore the central angle ∠BOC = 180° - 56° - 56° = 68°. Angle A, i.e. ∠BAC, is an inscribed angle subtending chord/arc BC, so it equals half the central angle ∠BOC. Thus ∠A = 68°/2 = 34°.
